issues.t: V8 burns oil and smokes on startup
issues.sym: A puff of blue-gray smoke from the exhaust right after a cold start, and you need to add oil between changes, sometimes a quart every 1,000–2,000 miles.
issues.why: The valve stem seals on the twin-turbo V8 harden from the heat packed into the engine's center, and oil seeps past them into the cylinders where it burns.
issues.next: Check the oil level at every fill-up and never let it run low. Ask a BMW specialist to confirm where the oil is going; replacing the seals is a big engine-in-car job, so get a written quote.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets
issues.sym: A burning-oil smell after driving, oily residue on the side of the engine, or drops under the front of the SUV.
issues.why: The plastic valve cover with its built-in gasket, and the oil filter housing and filler gaskets, harden with heat and start to seep, usually from around 40,000 miles.
issues.next: Have a shop find the exact source. Oil dripping onto the hot exhaust can smoke and is a fire risk, so do not leave a steady leak for long.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the expansion tank and plastic hoses
issues.sym: Low coolant warning, a sweet smell, pink or blue crust around the coolant tank, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The plastic expansion tank and coolant hoses on the 6-cylinder become brittle with age and heat and crack, usually somewhere between 60,000 and 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Top up only with BMW-approved coolant and get the leak found quickly. If the temperature warning comes on, pull over and shut the engine off to avoid engine damage.

issues.t: V8 rear coolant pipe leaks
issues.sym: Coolant loss with no obvious drip, a coolant smell near the back of the engine bay or from the vents, and in time a low-coolant warning.
issues.why: The coolant crossover pipe at the back of the V8 sits deep under the intake and turbos. Its seals leak with age, and the tight spot makes it hard to reach.
issues.next: Have a cooling-system pressure test done. Because the V8 already runs hot, keep a close eye on coolant level until it is fixed.

issues.t: V8 turbo oil feed lines leak
issues.sym: Oil residue around the turbochargers, a hot-oil smell, or smoke rising from the engine bay after a drive.
issues.why: The oil lines that feed the two turbos sit right next to them inside the V. Constant heat breaks down the seals and lines over time.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and fixed before it gets worse; oil on hot turbo parts can catch fire.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump wears out
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation or stumbling when you press the gas, long cranking before it starts, and a check engine light with fuel pressure codes.
issues.why: The engine-driven high-pressure fuel pump wears internally and can no longer keep up fuel pressure, usually somewhere between 50,000 and 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure codes read. If the pump is weak the engine may go into reduced-power mode, so book the repair soon.

issues.t: V8 fuel injectors fail and cause misfires
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, a flashing or steady check engine light, and loss of power, often on one cylinder.
issues.why: The direct-injection injectors on the twin-turbo V8 wear out and leak or stick, typically from about 60,000 miles.
issues.next: A flashing check engine light means a misfire that can damage the catalytic converters, so drive gently to a shop. Injectors are often replaced as a set.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor wears out
issues.sym: A suspension warning on the dash, the SUV slow to rise after starting, a sagging corner, or a compressor that runs and buzzes often.
issues.why: The air suspension compressor is a wear part. It works harder as the system ages and eventually can no longer build pressure, often around 50,000–80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the system scanned to tell a leaking air strut from a tired compressor. Replacing a compressor without fixing a leak will just wear out the new one.

issues.t: Air struts leak and one corner sags
issues.sym: One corner sits lower after the SUV is parked overnight, the ride height looks uneven, or the compressor keeps cycling.
issues.why: The rubber bag in an air strut cracks with age, more so in cold climates, and slowly lets air out.
issues.next: If one corner drops a lot, avoid long drives until it is checked. Replacing the strut early also protects the compressor.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings wear and clunk
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a loose or vague feel in the steering, or uneven tire wear on the front.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms carry this heavy SUV's weight and wear out, often between 40,000 and 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and get an alignment after the repair. It is not an emergency but worn bushings get worse and eat tires.

issues.t: iDrive screen freezes or reboots
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, goes black, or restarts on its own while driving; navigation, audio or the camera may drop out for a minute.
issues.why: The pre-facelift iDrive 7 software had bugs, with 2019 models reporting the most. Most cases are fixed with a software update.
issues.next: Ask a BMW dealer to check for and install the latest software. If it keeps happening after updates, the head unit itself may need to be replaced.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains and triggers warnings
issues.sym: Several warning messages at once, features that don't wake up, slow cranking, or a dead battery after the SUV sits.
issues.why: These SUVs have a heavy electrical load, and an aging 12-volt battery can no longer keep up, usually after 4–6 years. Control units then report odd faults.
issues.next: Have the battery tested before chasing other warnings. A new battery must be registered to the car with a scan tool.

issues.t: Power windows stick up or down
issues.sym: A window stops moving, moves slowly, or makes a grinding noise; it may get stuck open.
issues.why: The window motor or regulator inside the door fails.
issues.next: If a window is stuck open, cover it to keep weather out and have the motor or regulator replaced.

issues.t: Integrated brake unit can lose power assist and ABS (recall)
issues.sym: Brake or stability-control warnings, and a brake pedal that suddenly feels hard and needs much more force to stop the SUV.
issues.why: The integrated brake system that combines the brake booster with ABS and stability control can malfunction; on some units, welds in its motor can break. BMW has issued several recalls for it (24V-104, 24V-697, 24V-739 and 26V-422), and cars fixed under an earlier one may need the newer repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls even if the car was repaired before. If brake warnings appear, drive slowly with extra stopping distance straight to a dealer, or have it towed.

issues.t: Brake unit rotor and shaft can separate (recall)
issues.sym: ABS and brake warning lights and noticeably weaker braking, most likely after a hard stop.
issues.why: On some brake units, the rotor and shaft inside were not welded properly and can come apart under hard braking (recall 21V-062).
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether your SUV is covered and get the unit replaced for free.

issues.t: Starter can overheat after repeated start attempts (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or the starter clicks; after several tries you may smell something hot or burning.
issues.why: If the starter has already failed, cranking again and again can overload and overheat it, which could ignite nearby material. A software update came first (24V-576), then a starter replacement (25V-644), including for cars that already got the update.
issues.next: Don't keep trying to start the engine if it won't turn over. Have it towed to a dealer and make sure both recall repairs are done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy from a mis-built dash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see. The problem shows up only in a crash.
issues.why: The instrument panel may have been assembled incorrectly, which can stop the passenger airbag from opening properly (recall 25V-837).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer replace the dashboard trim for free.

issues.t: Windshield seal can let water into the electronics (recall)
issues.sym: Damp carpet or water near the front footwells, and electrical glitches such as headlights or other systems cutting out.
issues.why: The windshield may not be sealed properly, so rain can reach the power distribution box or a control unit, causing failures or a short circuit (recall 25V-556).
issues.next: If you notice water inside or odd electrical faults, park it outside and see a dealer. The reseal and any damaged electronics are fixed free.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Water leaks at the base of the windshield, wet carpets, or electrical problems after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Some xDrive40i windshields were not bonded correctly, letting water reach electrical parts and creating a short-circuit and fire risk (recall 22V-820).
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the seal; if needed they reinstall the windshield with a new seal for free.

issues.t: Knee airbags may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The problem appears only in a crash.
issues.why: Driver and passenger knee airbags on some 2024 X7s may have been built wrong and may not inflate as designed (recalls 23V-471 and 23V-622).
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the dealer replace the knee airbags for free.

issues.t: Dashboard may break apart when the airbag deploys (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you would notice while driving.
issues.why: On some 2024 xDrive40i models the instrument panel may not have been made properly, so in a crash the airbag may not work as intended or pieces of the panel could fly off (recall 24V-138).
issues.next: Have the dealer replace the instrument panel for free.

issues.t: Seat belt sensor may think an empty belt is fastened (recall)
issues.sym: The seat belt reminder may stay off even when someone in front is not buckled.
issues.why: The front seat belt system can wrongly detect a buckled belt, so the reminder may not warn you and the airbag may not deploy as intended (recall 24V-345).
issues.next: Always buckle up regardless of the warning light, and have the dealer inspect and replace the lower belt parts for free.

issues.t: Exhaust pipe fasteners at the converter may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, a ticking or puffing noise, or an exhaust or burning smell.
issues.why: On some 2023 M60i models, the fasteners joining the exhaust to the catalytic converter may not have been tightened correctly, creating a fire risk (recall 23V-294).
issues.next: If you smell exhaust or burning, stop and have it checked. The dealer replaces the gasket and tightens the fasteners for free.

issues.t: Only one front parking light may stay on (recall)
issues.sym: In some situations only one of the front parking lights is lit.
issues.why: A software fault in the light control unit can leave one front parking light off, which fails federal lighting rules (recall 22V-725).
issues.next: Have the dealer reprogram the light control unit; it's free and quick.

issues.t: Sunroof can close without the key inside (recall)
issues.sym: The panoramic sunroof can be closed from inside even when the key fob isn't in the SUV.
issues.why: The roof control unit was programmed wrong, so the sunroof's anti-trap rules were not met and a child could be caught by a closing roof (recall 22V-267).
issues.next: Never leave children alone in the SUV, and have the dealer reprogram the roof module for free.

issues.t: Third-row seatback may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: The third-row backrest may not latch firmly upright.
issues.why: Springs that lock the third-row backrest may be missing or installed wrong, so the seat may not hold in a crash (recall 22V-670).
issues.next: Check that third-row seatbacks click into place, and have the dealer inspect and fix the springs for free.

issues.t: Second-row head restraints may be the wrong type (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing obvious.
issues.why: Some 2021 X7s got the wrong outer head restraints in the second row, and they could come off in a crash (recall 21V-156).
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the head restraints for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be blocked or blank (recalls)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the camera picture is partly covered, missing, or the screen stays dark.
issues.why: Software problems could hide the rear camera view or keep the screen from showing it (recalls 19V-684 and 21V-096).
issues.next: Look over your shoulder and use the mirrors while reversing, and get the free camera software update.

issues.t: Steering column joint bolt may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness in the steering wheel, or play before the wheels respond.
issues.why: The bolt on the steering shaft's universal joint may not have been tightened enough and can work loose (recall 21V-031).
issues.next: If the steering feels loose, stop driving and have it towed. The dealer replaces and tightens the bolt or the joint for free.

issues.t: 48-volt battery cable connection can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly a hot or burning smell, or electrical warnings.
issues.why: On some 2021 xDrive40i models, the connection between the 48-volt battery and the starter-generator was assembled badly, raising resistance and fire risk (recall 20V-761).
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the connection for free; if you smell burning, stop and shut off the engine.

issues.t: Front axle support weld can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end and handling that feels off or uneven.
issues.why: The weld joining the front axle support to the right front control arm bracket may separate (recall 20V-678).
issues.next: Have the dealer check and replace the front axle support for free.

issues.t: Steering rack pinion teeth can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or free play in the steering and a steering warning light; in the worst case steering control is lost.
issues.why: Teeth on the steering rack's pinion gear can break under load (recall 19V-631).
issues.next: If the steering feels wrong, don't drive it. The dealer replaces the steering rack for free.

issues.t: Headlights may shine a bluish light (recall)
issues.sym: The headlights look noticeably blue to other drivers.
issues.why: Some M50i headlamps give off blue light that doesn't meet federal lighting rules and can confuse oncoming drivers (recall 20V-528).
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the headlamps for free.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: On some 2019 xDrive50i models, the V8's high-pressure fuel pump may not have been fastened correctly, so its flange can crack and leak fuel near hot parts (recall 19V-513).
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and call a dealer; the pumps are replaced for free.

issues.t: Head airbags may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing visible in daily use.
issues.why: The side curtain (head) airbags may not have been lined up with the trim during assembly, which could hurt how they open (recall 19V-386).
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and reinstall the head airbags if needed, free.
